Duncan Trussell and Christopher Ryan share episode 468 of the Joe Rogan Experience, an early freewheeling entry from the show's young days. Ryan wrote Sex at Dawn, a challenge to standard views of human mating. Trussell brought the comedy and the cosmic streak. Rogan refereed his two friends.

The talk bounces between sex, drugs, death, and what it means to live a natural life in an unnatural age. Ryan argues his book's case while Trussell turns it into jokes and koans. The episode captures the show's early house style: smart friends, no plan, and hours of talk that feel like a great night.
podcast-tuckercarlson-NObi_e3yf3U:
Tucker Carlson opens by faulting Western coverage of the Ukraine war. He says most reporters stayed tied to Kyiv and its partners. They took official lines, he argues, for three long years.

Reporter Patrick Lancaster works from the other side of the lines. He films towns and troops under Russian control. The title promises what viewers are not told at home. Lancaster shares scenes and claims from the front. The episode offers a rare ground view that clashes with nightly news, for listeners who want both sides before judging. His footage shows war without a studio filter.
